title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation with `fermi`: The Chicago Piano Tuners Example
text: fermi package supports Bayesian Fermi estimation: breaking uncertain quantities components (decomposition), expressing beliefs probability distributions (priors), building uncertainty final estimates. vignette demonstrates classic Fermi problem: > many piano tuners Chicago? : Decompose problem. Construct expert-driven priors. Run Bayesian Fermi simulation. Summarise visualise resulting distribution.
code: library(fermi)

what: How many piano tuners are in Chicago?
title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation with `fermi`: The Chicago Piano Tuners Example
text: didn’t access data, estimate number piano tuners Chicago? Fermi estimate breaks problem smaller components can estimated easily. combine estimates get final answer. Bayesian version approach encodes uncertainty component probability distribution (prior). use Monte Carlo simulation propagate uncertainty calculation, resulting probability distribution final estimate. First, need decompose problem breaking smaller parts. decomposition use : tuners=populationpeople per household×fraction households piano×tunings per piano per year/(working days per year×tunings per tuner per day). \text{tuners} = \frac{   \text{population} }{   \text{people per household} } \times \text{fraction households piano} \times \text{tunings per piano per year} \;\Big/\; \left(   \text{working days per year}   \times   \text{tunings per tuner per day} \right).

what: Simulate the number of piano tuners (with uncertainty)
title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation with `fermi`: The Chicago Piano Tuners Example
text: priors place, can now simulate components. function passed bf_fermi_simulate() mirrors decomposition .
code: tuner_draws <- bf_fermi_simulate(   components = list(     pop = population_prior,     hh_size = hh_size_prior,     piano_frac = piano_frac_prior,     tunes_per_piano = tunes_per_piano_prior,     work_days = work_days_prior,     tunes_day = tunes_day_prior   ),   fun = function(     population,     hh_size,     piano_frac,     tunes_per_piano,     work_days,     tunes_day   ) {     (population / hh_size) *       piano_frac *       tunes_per_piano /       (work_days * tunes_day)   },   n_draws = 20000 )

text: Use Beta–Binomial model : unknown quantity probability (e.g. proportion users click button). data counts successes number trials. Trials can treated independent underlying probability. Mathematically: Prior:p∼Beta(α,β) p \sim \mathrm{Beta}(\alpha, \beta) Data:y∣p∼Binomial(n,p) y \mid p \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(n, p) Posterior:p∣y∼Beta(α+y,β+n−y) p \mid y \sim \mathrm{Beta}(\alpha + y,\; \beta + n - y) posterior functional form prior. ’s “conjugate” means .

previous_headings: 2. beta_gamma_posterior(): learning a rate of counts
title: Conjugate updates with `fermi`: Beta–Binomial, Gamma–Poisson, and Normal–Normal
text: Use Gamma–Poisson model : unknown quantity rate λ\lambda events per unit exposure (per day, per month, per person-year, etc.). Data counts events, often associated exposure (e.g. days observed, people risk). Mathematically: Prior: λ∼Gamma(α,β)\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha, \beta) Data: yi∣λ∼Poisson(λ⋅ei)y_i \mid \lambda \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda \cdot e_i), eie_i exposure observation ii. Posterior: λ∣y∼Gamma(α+∑yi,β+∑ei)\lambda \mid y \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha + \sum y_i,\; \beta + \sum e_i) useful whenever ’re counting random events time space.

title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation in R
text: R package helps make probabilistic estimates using Fermi method. allows break complex problems smaller, manageable variables calculate probability distribution outcome using Monte Carlo simulations. Whether ’re estimating market size, potential impacts policy change, number piano tuners Chicago, tool provides rigorous yet accessible way handle uncertainty.

title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation in R
text: can install development version fermi GitHub :
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("humaniverse/fermi")

title: Bayesian Fermi Estimation in R
text: Let’s say want estimate annual number dwelling fires England. can decompose problem follows: number dwelling fires=number dwellings×rate dwelling fires \text{number dwelling fires} = \text{number dwellings} \times \text{rate dwelling fires} number dwellings can decomposed : number dwellings=population×average household size \text{number dwellings} = \text{population} \times \text{average household size} express beliefs component using probability distributions (priors), use fermi package simulate overall distribution dwelling fires:
code: library(fermi)  # ---- Priors ---- # Population of England, which we'll judge to be between 54 and 56 million with 80% credibility england_pop_prior <- expert_gamma_prior(   q = c(5.4e7, 5.6e7),   p = c(0.1, 0.9) )  # Average number of people in a household, judged to be between 2 and 3.2 with 80% credibility hh_size_prior <- expert_normal_prior(   mean = 2.4,   lower = 2.0,   upper = 3.2,   level = 0.8 )  # Risk of dwelling fires, judged to be between 0.01% and 0.06%, with 80% credibility fire_rate_prior <- expert_beta_prior(   q = c(0.001, 0.006),   p = c(0.1, 0.9) )  # ---- Fermi simulation ---- fermi_res <- bf_fermi_simulate(   components = list(     pop = england_pop_prior,     hh_size = hh_size_prior,     p_fire = fire_rate_prior   ),   # This is where we define how the components combine to give the final estimate   fun = function(pop, hh_size, p_fire) {     (pop / hh_size) * p_fire   },   n_draws = 20000 )  # Summarise and plot posterior_summary(fermi_res, cred_level = 0.89) #> Posterior summary #>   Credible level: 89 % #>   Median        : 65294.03  #>   CI            : [16335.58, 175730.8] #>   HDI           : [5916.407, 145177.3]  plot_posterior(fermi_res, cred_level = 0.89)
